root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix an integer n greater than 1. Define f(x) = floor of n times x minus the sum from k = 1 to n of (floor of k times x) divided by k. Determine the set of real numbers x for which f(x) is a global maximum among all real y, and determine the value of that global maximum.
quantifier_order: for a given integer n greater than 1
find real x such that for all real y, expression at x is at least the expression at y
and there exists at least one real x achieving that maximal value

payload.theorem_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: First use integer-shift invariance to replace x by its fractional part r in [0,1). On [0,1), compare r to the left endpoint m/n of its n-slice, where m = floor(nr). The last slice [(n-1)/n,1) is computed explicitly and yields the value H_n - 1. Every lower slice has value strictly below H_n - 1 by the discrete bottleneck lemma. Hence the maximum is H_n - 1, and the maximizers are exactly the integer translates of [(n-1)/n,1).

steps.derives: For any real x, f_n(x) depends only on frac(x), so it suffices to maximize over r = frac(x) with 0 <= r < 1.
steps.trivial_justification: This is a direct application of the fractional-part reduction lemma and the standard property 0 <= frac(x) < 1.

steps.derives: For r in [0,1), letting m = floor(n*r), one has f_n(r) <= f_n(m/n).
If r lies in [(n-1)/n, 1), then f_n(r) = H_n - 1.
If r < (n-1)/n, then m = floor(n*r) <= n-2, so f_n(r) <= f_n(m/n) < H_n - 1.

Therefore the global maximum value is H_n - 1, and the maximizing real numbers are exactly those x whose fractional part lies in [(n-1)/n, 1), equivalently x in the union over integers z of [z + (n-1)/n, z + 1).
